user_query: How does LINE(2nd) on the reconstructed Youtube network compare with DeepWalk across the degree groups, and what does the reconstructed dense network change?
llm_response: On the reconstructed YouTube network, LINE(2nd) is generally competitive with DeepWalk but tends to be slightly worse in the lower-degree groups and closer to DeepWalk in the higher-degree groups. In other words, DeepWalk usually has the edge for sparse/low-degree nodes, while LINE(2nd) narrows the gap as degree increases. The reconstructed dense network changes this pattern by making the graph much more connected, which reduces the disadvantage of low-degree nodes and makes the performance across degree groups more uniform; as a result, the difference between LINE(2nd) and DeepWalk becomes smaller and the degree-based variation is less pronounced.
llm_confidence_reasoning: This is a high-level synthesis of the reported degree-group trend and the effect of densifying the reconstructed network, but the exact per-group values are not available here, so some wording is necessarily approximate.
